statement: A secret shown in dispute arguments is learned by every hosted Entity, as one shown by SecretRevealed is. The chain pays a payment clause when its secret is in the arguments of a dispute op before the clause's deadline (DeltaTransformer applyPayment, 294-299) and logs no SecretRevealed for it, so a hub that forwarded the lock would fail it back upstream while the payee was paid downstream. Two places carry such arguments. DisputeStarted logs the starter's two argument blobs (initial and counter) in its own data, so the watcher reads their secrets from the log. DisputeFinalized logs only finalizationEvidenceHash, a hash of the initial body hash, the final nonce, both sides, and the hashes of the starter's blob, the other side's blob and the signature; the blobs are in the input of the transaction. The Host fetches the input of each transaction that carried a finalize (eth_getTransactionByHash, once per transaction per poll; a node that cannot give it is a port fault, tried again at the next tick, nothing delivered), reads it with the ABI cursors as the contract reads it (processBatch, then the batch's finalize ops), and takes the secrets of the op whose evidence hash is the logged one, from both blobs: the evidence hash authenticates the op, so a secret is never taken from an op the log is not about. A blob is `abi.encode(Arguments{uint16[] fillRatios; bytes32[] secrets})`; a blob that is not that has no secrets (the contract reads it as empty). Each secret is told as `j_secret` to every hosted Entity, ahead of the event that follows it: a start's before its j_dispute, a finalize's before the epoch advance the finalize made (so before the holds that advance dissolves, R-HOLD-DISSOLVE; a finalize with no advance in the batch tells them before itself). The Entity's paybook turns a secret into a pass-up by its hash on any Account (R-DISPUTE-FREEZE), so a secret that opens no lock it forwarded changes nothing. A finalize whose input is not a processBatch call (a contract that wrapped it) or holds no op with the logged hash cannot be read: its parties are told `j_finalize_unread` (notice `finalize_unread`, no fact changes) after `j_dispute_over`, so the owner knows a secret may have been shown unseen; the watcher is not stopped for it, because a counterparty could wrap a finalize on purpose. A secret shown in the starter's counter blob is read though the chain uses that blob only if the counter is the one selected: reading more only hands a hub a real preimage. Not here: the body of a proof from a start's or a counter's calldata (the finalized offdelta in the notices, ACCEPT with a body the node cannot rebuild: owed), a finalize carried by a call that is not processBatch (not read: told as unread), and secrets in a counter dispute (a counter proof carries no arguments).
source: Review A B4 on #162; coordinator audit of #162 (A: calldata PR); DeltaTransformer.sol 294-299; Depository.sol finalizationEvidenceHash (975-1006); builder 10-02

killers.name: R-WATCH-CALLDATA the secrets of an Arguments blob are read in order, and none from what is not one
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a dispute start shows the secrets of both its blobs, each once
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a processBatch input gives each finalize op with the evidence hash the chain logs
R-WATCH-CALLDATA an input that is not a processBatch call, or is cut short, has no finalize ops
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a finalize count the input has no room for gives no ops, and no list is built for it
R-WATCH-CALLDATA the secrets of a finalize are those of the op whose evidence hash was logged
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a finalize's secrets are told to every hosted Entity before the epoch advance it made
R-WATCH-CALLDATA the starter's arguments at a finalize are shown too, and the op is found among others
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a finalize with no advance before it tells its own secrets, just ahead of itself
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a dispute start's secrets are told ahead of the dispute, with no input needed
R-WATCH-CALLDATA the Host is asked for the input of each transaction that carried a finalize, once
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a finalize whose input cannot be read is told to its parties and shows no secret
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a finalize the Host has not asked about says nothing of its arguments
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a finalize's arguments are read from its transaction's input, asked for once
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a dispute start's arguments show their secret to the Entity, no input asked for
R-WATCH-CALLDATA an input the node cannot give is the port's fault: nothing is delivered
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a transaction is asked for by hash and its input comes back as bytes
R-WATCH-CALLDATA a finalize the Host could not read is told as a notice, and no fact changes
